description: Mobile CapCut tutorial showing palette-based color changes, shape masks and opacity controls, intercut with finished examples.

techniques.name: Palette-guided color adjustment
techniques.evidence: The palette image and a before/after tinted portrait appear alongside CapCut color controls.
implementation: Choose a coherent palette separately from the source image.
Use original colors in newly created graphics; do not reuse the example portrait or film stills.

techniques.name: Shape-mask composition
techniques.evidence: Mask controls show a yellow circle and a circular portrait crop.
implementation: Use an ellipse mask for a supplied image.
Animate the mask or scale using deterministic easing.
Keep controls and timeline outside the generated composition.

techniques.name: Opacity keyframes
techniques.evidence: The opacity slider and diamond keyframe markers are visible in the final sampled section.
implementation: Interpolate opacity from absolute timeline time.

typography: Instructional labels surround example footage; labels belong to the tutorial, not the desired output.
composition: Portrait screen recording; the preview is above the toolbar and timeline.
effects: Color adjustment, circular clipping and opacity are visibly demonstrated.
easing: Exact source interpolation is uncertain. Any stored guidance is an original cubic-ease design recommendation, not a recovered curve.

tutorial.interface: Mobile CapCut preview, filters/adjustment toolbar, mask picker and timeline are visible.
tutorial.animationRegions: The source media in the upper preview, excluding the timeline, buttons and instructional captions.
steps: Find a color palette and compare it with the original footage.
Open color adjustment controls; exact numeric settings are unreadable.
Choose a circle mask for a layer and position the crop.
Add opacity changes with timeline keyframes.
tutorial.limitations: No audio transcription; tap order between sampled frames and exact settings are uncertain.

uncertainties: Exact font family and original keyframe/easing parameters are not recoverable from these sampled frames.
Intervals are approximate observations, not audio-aligned or frame-precise annotations.
reviewer: Codex visual review of sampled source frames
